title: Transport for the Malta trip (13–19 October 2026)
intro: Start with current organizer instructions and the visible dated agenda; only 14–16 October entries were visible in the 11 October listing read. Route 186 and Route 214 are public-bus candidates between Qawra and the Ta’ Qali event area, not confirmed hotel-to-gate journeys. An Eventbrite listing read 11 October gives the venue address and coordinates and publishes agenda times for 14–16 October; the traveler’s own reservation, gate, 17–18 October agenda and exact route remain unconfirmed. MPT’s fare table lists seasonal single prices (€2.50 summer / €2.00 winter) and card products; its stated winter-single period ends 13 June 2026, but third-party 2026 fare guides place the season boundary at 18/19 October, so the likely fares are €2.50 on 13–18 October and €2.00 on 19 October (partially verified inference — confirm with MPT). The operator’s Route 186 page lists the last Stadium 2194 departures toward Buġibba at 20:53/20:54; run the date-specific planner in both directions, check the later leads (Route 202 toward Sliema; N48/N212 night chains), and keep a live-quote taxi/ride-hailing alternative for a late finish, especially on 17 October. A separate notice closes Saqqajja stop 4627 on Route 186 until a printed January 1 with no year. An earlier same-day stop trace places it before Stadium 2194 on the return, not at the boarding stop; this pass did not re-walk that chain.

records.description: Route 186 runs between Rabat and Buġibba and is the operator- and venue-endorsed link from the Buġibba/Qawra side to the Ta' Qali Stadium stop, but it is ASYMMETRIC and that is the single most important transport fact for this trip. On the operator's own stop lists the direction that serves Il-Qawra's seafront stops (Arznell 950, Luzzu 951, Qawra 952) runs inland toward Ta' Qali and Rabat, while the return from the opposite-side Stadium stop lists no Il-Qawra stop at all and finishes at Buġibba. A return by Route 186 therefore ends in Buġibba rather than at the hotel door, and the last useful departure is variant-dependent: the operator publishes the Stadium stop with last times of 20:53/20:54 in one unlabelled grid and 22:04/22:08 in others, so confirm the actual date instead of trusting a single figure. The Qawra seafront stop is published up to 21:39 in the series read. Fixed facts worth relying on: the route exists, it takes about 25–33 minutes from the Qawra stops to the Stadium stop, and it runs on a repeating 30-minute headway. Everything about the exact last return needs a same-day check.
records.notes: Operator route page with the stop-by-stop grids, read 11 October 2026: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ . Stops confirmed in that page’s lists: Il-Qawra Arznell 950, Luzzu 951, Qawra 952, Ta’ Qali Gibjun 6118, Venture 6226, Stadium 6227 and Villagg 6228; Rabat 4 (2567) is the other terminus. The same page shows stops 6227/6228/2191 also served by Routes 56 and 202, and the Stadium 6227 stop is also listed for the Ta’ Qali Park & Ride shuttles 403, 404 and 405 — useful alternates to compare in the planner. Route 214 lists Qawra and Qali-area stops as a second option: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/214/ . For the Saturday 17 October evening diversion see the separate diversion record. Date-specific planner (not run here): https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ . The operator’s public notice of the 17 October diversion is at https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ . Second-session caveats (11 October 2026): the static page shows multiple time variants and earlier tighter bounds were withdrawn rather than presented as trip-day times; the date-specific planner is https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ . Return stop 2194 was independently re-read on 11 October; outbound 6227 and return 2194 are different direction stops, so no single clock range is asserted. Route 186 is a day route, so a single journey costs the day-route price and is covered by the 7-day Explore Adult card; the closest listed sales office to Qawra is the Buġibba Terminal: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/office-and-ticket-machine/ . Third-pass additions (11 October 2026): the full return chain toward Buġibba was traced stop by stop and contains no Il-Qawra stop — Rabat 2 (2569), Mdina (135), Saqqajja (4627), Qanpiena (2232), Telgha (2231), Snajja (2192), Villagg (2193), Stadium (2194), Venture (6134), Gibjun (4125), Ħ'Attard Sedqa (2457), Marg (2458), Gheneb (5674), Mosta Waqqafa (2196), Trincetta (2200), Gholja 2 (1101), Mithna (1099), Milt (1097), Gatt (1143), Kungress (1142), Rotunda 2 (2563), Isouard (1105), Kostituzzjoni (1106), Targa (1107), Gharusa (1200), Rihana (1202), Campra (1203), Ramez (1204), Burmarrad (1205), Qannotta (1206), Qadi (1207), Mwiezeb (956), Imhasel (958), Toni (6013), Gillieru (6014), Moll (6193), Rizzi (946), Sajf (947), Gzejjer (948), Buġibba Bay 1 (2527). Buġibba Bay 1 arrival is read as 21:26 in one variant and 21:36 in another on the same page, and a single 21:27 figure also appears in this dataset's event-day record; the variants are not labelled, so a range is reported and NO single clock time should be asserted. The mandatory onward transfer is recorded separately as route-186-return-transfer-bugibba. Two-hour transfer validity: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ . Two independent corroborations added by a parallel session and folded in here: BLAST's own attendee guide names “Malta Fairs & Conventions Centre – BLAST Arena Studios” at “Ta Qali, ATD 4000 Ħ’Attard”, which resolves the traveller-supplied “Attard” and the Ta’ Qali references as the SAME venue (see `blast-arena-studios-venue-address`), so routing to the Ta’ Qali Stadium stops is correct; and MFCC's own venue booklet states “BY BUS - FROM VALLETTA no.56, FROM SLIEMA no.202, FROM BUGIBBA no.186” (see `mfcc-official-bus-186`), making Route 186 venue-endorsed from the Buġibba/Qawra side as well as operator-listed. Neither corroborates the attendee gate or door times. Second read on 11 October 2026 (later in the same day) confirmed the outbound side of the grids: Qawra 952 shows a 30-minute pattern from 06:09 with a last departure of 21:39, Stadium 6227 last 22:04 on one grid and 22:08 on the second grid on the same page, and Rabat 4 (2567) last 22:13/22:18 — so the two unlabelled variants differ by about four to five minutes at the venue stop. The return grid was not re-extracted in that second read; the 20:53/20:54 Stadium 2194 departures and the 21:26/21:36 Buġibba Bay 1 arrivals remain as read earlier the same day. Reproducibility caveat added after integrating a parallel 11 October session: that session's reads of the Route 186 page (stop index chunks 1–3 and timetable chunks 12, 13 and 15) did not reproduce the 2194/20:53–20:54 return row, and this session's own read of a later chunk reproduced only the opposite (toward-Rabat) direction. The figure comes from an earlier 11 October read of the same paginated page, so treat it as a published-grid value that needs confirmation — what is robust is the direction problem (the return terminates at Buġibba Bay 1, not Qawra) and the need to check the date-specific planner, not the exact last minute.

TQ2, TQ3 and TQ4 are also listed in the operator's route directory. The corridor and the event-only nature of these routes are documented by a public route list, which describes special one-off services organised after major events such as festivals and concerts, announced a few days beforehand, and gives TQ1 as Ta' Qali → Rabat, Mosta, Naxxar, St. Paul's Bay, Qawra → Buġibba: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_bus_routes_in_Malta . Special Services fare €3.00 and card inclusions are from the operator's fare page: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ . NO TWC-specific special service was found on 11 Oct 2026 and none is assumed. Monitor https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ and the tallinja app; if nothing is announced, use the taxi plan in the late-return entry. Current integration recheck read route-page chunks 0 and 6, including the final “Timetable not available!” message. The intervening all-network stop selector was not read; it is not a TQ1 stop list. Historical route/report evidence was not freshly re-opened. Re-opened again later on 11 October 2026: the TQ1 page still ended with 'Timetable not available!', and the operator's full latest-service-updates page read at the same check published no TQ service and no Thunderpick/BLAST event notice. Two days before the event this remains the single most useful thing to recheck daily, because a TQ service through Qawra is the only published corridor that could remove the late-return taxi requirement. Third read on 11 October 2026 added two published route definitions and one dated precedent, still without any Thunderpick announcement. The route definitions come from the Wikipedia list of Maltese bus routes' special-services table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_bus_routes_in_Malta): 'TQ1 (Northern Route) | Ta' Qali | via Rabat, Mosta, Naxxar, St. Paul's Bay, Qawra | Buġibba' and 'TQ2 (Central Route) | Ta' Qali | via Lija, Birkirkara (Bypass), San Ġwann, St Julian's, Sliema | Valletta'; a 2023 Earth Garden special-service report used the same two route names and stop sequences (https://newsbook.com.mt/en/malta-public-transport-provides-special-service-for-earth-garden-2023/). The precedent is MPT's own announced 2026 national-stadium service: for the Malta v Luxembourg play-off it ran extra trips on key routes from Valletta, Buġibba, Sliema and the University, made regular and special services free for Tallinja card holders, charged €2 on board for everyone else, and stationed buses close to the stadium after the final whistle departing to Valletta, Sliema, St Paul's Bay, Żurrieq and Paola 'depending on demand' (https://lovinmalta.com/news/local/malta-public-transport-to-run-special-bus-services-for-malta-vs-luxembourg-play-off/). That is a news report about a March 2026 football match, not a published TWC service: it shows the Ta' Qali post-event Bus-and-Buġibba pattern exists when MPT chooses to run it, and nothing more. The 11 October three-chunk re-read of the operator's updates page still contained no TWC, BLAST or TQ notice, so the late-return question stays open and any special service would be announced only days beforehand.
